utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may be seated. Mrs. Klipic, you understand that you are still under oath, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mrs. Klipic, yesterday you said in your evidence how the people came down from the hill towards Kozarac and then the column moved up towards the town of Kozarusa. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That this took a considerable period of time because some people were walking and some were travelling in motorized vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was the nationality of the people in the column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were all Muslim, except for one Serb named Mirko.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you got to Kozarusa, apart from the people being sorted out into the various different categories, those going to Keraterm, Omarska, Trnopolje, was anything else done with the people at that point, that you could remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean, where were they taken or?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were they searched?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were all searched, women and men were searched.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I see. Were any of the people in that column carrying arms that you were able to see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Serbs had arms but not us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes. The people in the column, I said, the people in the column were not armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were any of the people in the column offering any resistance to the Serbs, as they brought them down to this place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had no arms because everyone who had arms, weapons, surrendered them to the Police and to the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you look at the photograph, please, that I now show you? Might the copy be marked, please, but the original photograph shown to the witness? Do you recognise the photograph that I am now showing you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is my brother, my older brother, Envir Alic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I tender that photograph, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection? That is Prosecution Exhibit 213, I believe. Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It is No. Z5/25 for the benefit of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 213 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Could the photograph itself, the original photograph, be put on the screen, please? Thank you. Could it be expanded to the fullest size that it can be done? (To the witness): Just looking at that photograph on this video monitor, the video projector, not on the screen in front of you, could you point to your brother, please, with the pointer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my brother Eno, Enver Alic, my older brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who is the lady that sits beside him there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is his wife, Kelima.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: She is nursing a child, is she?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is their daughter, Azra. She is now 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did your brother, Enver, have a nickname by which he was known?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they called him "Eno".

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When was he born, can you remember?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: His ethnic group is Muslim, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So far as you are aware, is he still alive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not believe so. I do not know. My father took out my brother, Enver, from the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your father was with Enver in Omarska, was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you ask your father whether he knew whether he was still alive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My father, perhaps, is trying to console us but he always says: "You should know Eno is not here any more."

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So far as you know, did he die or has he disappeared when he was in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, my father brought Eno into a garage or a house, I am not sure what was it, and Jasko, Emir was there. My father was returned after he brought my brother to that room and -----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can I raise a matter of objection here, your Honour? There is no evidence that this lady was in the place to which this incident refers which is the camp at Omarska. As I understand it, the Prosecution are now through her adducing evidence of what has been told by her father to her. In our submission, that contravenes rules that would be usually applied in many courts concerning hearsay. Perhaps the Prosecution should argue before this court why this evidence should be adduced in this form, and the court hear submissions on behalf of the Defence about this matter.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Once again, I suppose, when you make your objection on the ground of hearsay, I always responded by saying that our 10 rules of evidence do not prohibit the admission of hearsay. That is not dealt with. Instead, the standard is relevant evidence that has probative value. I will accept that your argument would be that, even though that is the case, this lacks probative value, although it may not be appropriate for me to think that is your submission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is the foundation of it. I would be happier if there was a debate -- submissions, rather than debate.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You mean filings, written filings?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exactly, your Honour, if this is to be the course that the Prosecution are going to seek to use in adducing evidence in this case. It is quite plainly the case and I, of course, have had a statement from the Prosecution in relation to what she proposed to say, and I know she was not in Omarska camp. What the court has heard and the transcript I have, no doubt, clearly shows is that this is information given to her by her father who was there.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. I am not seeking to lead from this evidence what it was that actually happened. The whole purpose of the questions is to elicit from the witness whether or not she knows whether her brother is alive, what enquiry she has made. It goes to the issue of proof of death. I am not seeking to go any further than that. It is merely just a question of did she know from her enquiries where he died and did she make enquiries, and what the nature of the enquiries that she made. She made enquiries of her father and what is her belief as to where he died, that is, her brother. That is as far as I wish to take the evidence, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think she has already answered it. As far what her father told her -- the problem -- I almost said this is double hearsay, and Mr. Wladimiroff is looking at me, and I keep saying that that hearsay is not a problem, at least in terms of admission as hearsay before this Tribunal; the question is whether it has probative value. It is certainly relevant. I gather her brother is the person who is named in paragraph ---

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In the indictment.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: -- 6 of the indictment, so it is certainly relevant. The question is whether it has probative value. If you are offering it only on the question of death, and not as to who was responsible for that death, I do not know whether there will be much prejudice. Let me confer with my fellow Judges though and see. They tell me that they entirely agree with me, that is, it will come in, it is relevant, and it appears to have some probative value; that what is coming in is not evidence as to who was responsible for the death, but whether or not she believes he is dead and what is the basis for that thought. I will overrule your objection, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If your Honours, please. (To the witness): Do you remember the question? Excuse me, your Honours is quite right. I think the witness has answered the question so there is no necessity for me to take it any further, so I will not. That exhibit I tender and might it be marked 213?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: She did answer the question, as I recall. You were trying to determine what was the basis for her belief and I am not sure really whether you concluded it, but if you have concluded it, that is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I do not need to take it any further.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. MR. NIEMANN (To the witness): Would you look now, please, at the next photograph that I show you? Might the copy of this photograph be marked No. 214? Might the other photograph be returned to the Registrar, please, my copy? Just looking at the photograph I have now shown you, do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What is it a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It shows two policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know one of the policemen in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know Hajrudin Jakupovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I tender that photograph and, for the benefit of the Defence, your Honours, this is Z5-26.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 214 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps the photograph can be displayed on the screen? The person that you recognise in that photograph could you point to, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my relative and friend, Hajrudin Jakupovic, policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Have you made any enquiries as to whether he is dead or alive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. He was taken out of Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Has he been missing since the war in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not known.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, has he been missing since the war, so far as you are aware, in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So far as you know, did he go to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was told by my friend and neighbours who came back from Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When was he born, do you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was he Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did he live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He lived in Gornji Jakupovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Approximately how far is that from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately eight, nine kilometres, and he used to work in Kozarac for five or six years -- actually, may be more, seven or eight.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was his occupation in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He worked as a policeman, an active policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What uniform was he dressed in there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a winter uniform and our policemen also had a spring/summer uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is this the winter uniform of the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: This is the civilian police as opposed to military police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: This is a fairly old photograph, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think that this is the third or fourth year that he spent in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I tender that, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 214 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you look at the photograph that I now show you? Might the copy again be marked so that the original can be returned to the witness? Do you recognise that photograph? That photograph for the benefit of Defence is Z5-27. Do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who is it a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my relative, Esad Alic, a policeman from Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I tender that photograph, your Honours, and might it be marked 215?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 215 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Could it be placed on the screen, please? (To the witness): That is Esad Alic, he is a relative of yours. Where did he live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kamicani.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: As best you can, can you tell us approximately how far that is from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think three, three-and-a-half kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When was he born, when was he born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think in 55, 54, or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was he a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What is the uniform that he is dressed in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Like every other policemen in Kozarac, this is also a winter uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What colour is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Blue, just like any other police uniform, grey blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where was he on duty as a policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Since the war in 1992, have you ever seen him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did he go into Omarska, so far as you are aware?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not believe so, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you make any enquiries as to what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. His brother came from Omarska and said that they were taken away from Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: They have not been seen since -- he has not been seen since?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you look at the next photograph? Might that be returned to the Registrar? Might the next photograph be marked, the copy marked 216? Do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: For the benefit of the Defence, that is Z5-28. Do you recognise who it is in that photograph or who that is a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Muhamed Jakupovic, a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I tender that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 216 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Might it be placed on the screen, Exhibit 216, and blown up as best it can be? This is a photograph of Mohamed Jakupovic. Is he in any way related to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a relative.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Again, the uniform he is dressed in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was he Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know when he was born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where was he a police officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He worked in Prijedor as a traffic policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Have you seen him since the war in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he disappeared in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You made enquiries yourself as to his whereabouts after the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If you would look at the next photograph I show you, and might be marked 217 and it is Z5-22. Do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is a photograph of your husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is that an extract of Exhibit 211, the first photograph that I showed you yesterday? Has it been taken from that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was your husband born in 1965?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is he a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Has he been missing since that day in Kozarac on 27th -- sorry, I withdraw that. Has he been missing since the first attack on Kozarac in 1992, in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: He was a policeman as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I tender that photograph, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 217 will be admitted. What was the exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: 211, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 211. I think Judge Vohrah would like .....

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Displayed on the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Could it be displayed on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. NIEMANN (To the witness): Would you look at the next photograph that I show you, please? Do you recognise that photograph that you are shown?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: For the benefit of the Defence, that is Z5-23. Is that a photograph of your husband and his family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I tender that photograph, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is Exhibit 218, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to 218?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Could it be placed on the screen, please? (To the witness): Mrs. Klipic, your husband is the gentleman in uniform standing towards the centre of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is your father-in-law in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he is my father-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your father-in-law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is he in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is Fuad Klipic. He was killed in Trnopolje camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know when he was born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 41 or 42, I should say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you enquire about the circumstances of his death?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I went to Trnopolje and I was told by people who buried him and another individual from Kamicani.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know how he died?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not natural causes. I do not know how he was killed. Nobody could see that. They simply found him dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is your mother-in-law in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is my mother-in-law. She is alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I tender that, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That should be admitted 218, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: 218. (To the witness): Would you look now at the photographs I show you? Might the copy be marked 219? For the benefit of the Defence, that is Z5-24. Do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is a photograph of your brother, Ekrem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I tender that photograph, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 219 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Could it be placed on the screen, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is my brother Ekrem, Ekro. He disappeared from Benkovac on 27th, on Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is 27th May '92?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was he born in about 1955?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No -- 55, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: His nickname is Ekro?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Ekro.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was his occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My brother had a private business, he had his trucks and tractors and he worked with timber.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: At the time of his death, did you know whether he was engaged in military activity or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was not in the TO. He was a normal person like everybody else. I do not know how, could it be that we were organised? Had we been, all this would not have happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: He is Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I tender that, your Honour. Might exhibit 211 be returned to the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Can I just clarify something? That is a third brother, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Second brother, I think, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: A second brother?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, it is two brothers, Enver Alic and Ekrem Alic, and the other is her husband. Perhaps the photograph itself might be placed on the screen? (To the witness): This photograph we looked at yesterday, in the centre of the photograph is a photograph of your husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who is the gentleman sitting to the left of him? Can you see that gentleman there, if you could point to him first -- no, the other side.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is his brother, Fikret Klipic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know when he was born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fikret was born in 1960.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is he still alive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he is in Australia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps that exhibit might be returned? Mrs. Klipic, did you draw up a list of your relatives who are missing since the war in 1992 from the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How many of your relatives are missing since that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 35 of my relatives are missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: These relatives, were they a mixture of men, women and children or were they of the one sex?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, only men. I did not write down women and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know where these relatives were the last time you heard of them or heard from them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some were in Omarska, some in Benkovac, some in Trnopolje, Keraterm and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where is Benkovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Benkovac is up there close to Mrakovica. It is a youth village there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you also draw up a list of Muslim police officers that you knew that worked in the opstina Prijedor area that ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The list of policemen that you drew up, Muslim policemen, are these policemen that have not been heard of or seen since 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can I raise one matter here? My learned friend was good enough to discuss matters with the Defence this morning, and provided a list of names to us. I have had an opportunity now to reflect on the purpose of this evidence, and we object to it on this basis. It is a list of names who this lady has not heard of since May 1992. It is a general list of people generally in the area. We know that there was a great displacement of peoples. What I am concerned is that the case against Mr. Tadic is going to involve a list of names generally of people missing throughout the area, and obscure, perhaps, the issues in his case and the charges on the indictment that he faces and cause this court to be involved in matters that, perhaps, do not concern this prosecution. Perhaps the court would like to the opportunity to hear the foundation for it from my learned friend? But, as far as we are concerned, we think that this is evidence that really is too far in relation to this trial.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, you are the learned friend, would you like to respond?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, in relation to particularly the charge of persecution, there are allegations made of activities or policies directed against Muslims and/or non-Serbs in the area of Kozarac and the opstina of Prijedor. This evidence is presented in a number of ways. It is presented in relation to people specifically that we allege the accused was directly involved in their persecution. It is also on a more general basis, in our submission, because it is a policy directed towards the non-Serbs of the area. We submit that the reference to the people that she knows, whether they be relatives or whether they be policemen in the area, also goes to identifying some of the people, even if it is only by reference not particularly to the names, but even if it is just by reference to their category, it goes to this broader question of the persecution of the non-Serbs of the area.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you have anything further, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I understand the nature of the wider picture that the Prosecution are presenting as part of their case, but my concern is that that, perhaps, has already been achieved through witnesses that this court has heard over the previous five or six weeks; that what may be happening now is that the issues in relation to Mr. Tadic's case and the allegations specifically against him may be lost in relation to these more general matters.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We have heard a lot. That is for sure. One of the elements, well, one of the counts in the indictment is persecution. In that count it is alleged that there was a seizure and imprisonment of thousands of Muslims and Croats under brutal conditions located in Omarska and other camps, and then deportation or expulsion of the majority of Muslim and Croat residents of the opstina Prijedor by force or threat of force. The accused Mr. Tadic is named in that charge ---

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: -- and, obviously, there will have to be a connection between the deportation and expulsion which is alleged as one of the multiplicity of acts and Mr. Tadic, but this gets us to the first prong. I thought your concern might be that at least coming from this witness in this form it might be prejudicial and that it might be somewhat sensational, but this is a trial to the bench; I think that we are able to understand the nature of the testimony, who is giving it and the circumstances. But it certainly is relevant. To the extent that the witness can say that they are missing, I think that it is probative of that count. So I will overrule your objection and we will hear from the witness, but see if you can proceed more quickly, Mr. Niemann, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am much obliged.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. (To the witness): The policemen that were in that list you made enquiries of yourself to ascertain whether or not they had been missing since that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not your brother, Enver Alic, knew the accused, Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How is it that you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know because Dule Tadic, Vasa Crnogorac, Fadil Hrustic bought planks and various wooden elements for the coffee shop at my brother's. I saw them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You are saying your brother, Enver Alic, assisted with Dule Tadic's coffee shop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was building a house and everybody has helping him with these elements made of timber, so .....

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did your brother, Ekrem, so far as you know, know the accused Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Why is it that you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know because we all often went out to pubs and we all knew each other, my brother was also and Eno too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yesterday in your evidence you got to the point where you said that you went to Trnopolje. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I think you said you had your children with you at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: During the time that you were at Trnopolje, did you ever on any occasion see Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell the Tribunal when it is that you first saw Dule Tadic at the Trnopolje camp, when you were in Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my children were ill and I went from Trnopolje towards Trnjani, that is, towards Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I met him and Bolta again in a police Golf heading towards Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you walking at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was taking my two little sons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were they driving in the car at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was the car going fast or slow when it passed you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Slow, slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who was driving the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Brane Bolta.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where was the accused Dule Tadic sitting in the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was sitting next to him in the co-driver's seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: This was in the front of the car, the passenger's seat in the front of the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How far away were you from the car at the time when it became closest to you, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course, as they were coming, we met, we simply met. I was going towards Prijedor and they were going towards Trnopolje. They were going slowly and you see anything that comes towards you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you on the side of the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was walking in the opposite direction, not towards the car, but opposite the car, that is, I was going down the right-hand side of the road and he was also taking his right-hand side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What position on the road were you when you were walking down the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was between Trnjani and Trnopolje. It is about a kilometre, a kilometre-and-a-half. I do not remember exactly. I cannot remember the building that we met at, but I know exactly where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is the road sealed with bitumen at that point where you saw them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you walking on the part that was made of bitumen or were you walking on the gravel shoulder?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we were on the bitumen part. There was no sidewalks there. It was all bitumen, plain bitumen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see how the men were dressed in the car? Firstly, Bolta, how was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bolta was always dressed like this, as a policeman, and Dule was in camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection in your mind approximately when this was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was very soon in the beginning of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In early June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you have a clear view of Dule Tadic in that car as he approached you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I repeat it. Yes, I always say, yes, all I was interested was the police and not Dule, so Bolta and other policemen, I met Dusko too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you speak to Bolta on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes -- no, not then but we used to come across each other quite often at the SUP in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You said, I think, that you saw him on a second occasion. Can you tell us where that was that you saw him on the second occasion when you were in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was across the street from the school at Huskina pub in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: This is a hotel or a pub, is it, directly across from the Trnopolje school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is a private tavern, pub.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where were you standing or where were you at the time when you saw Dule Tadic on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was coming with my two sons because the children had fallen ill and they were losing liquid, and I had to go to Prijedor with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was this day-time or night-time when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Day-time, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you have a good view of Dule Tadic when you saw him on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was very close and very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you walking along the streets, were you, at this time when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was walking on foot and I was standing there. Zoka from the petrol station, Goran Babic, policeman, and one Mejakic and I know all those others, but I do not know their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How close did you get to Dule Tadic when you saw him on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were standing on one side of the bitumen and I passed by on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was your view of Dule Tadic obstructed in any way when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were very many policemen, many military, and I was going there to ask for an authorisation, to go for a permit, to go to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you at any stage cross the road and get closer to Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How was he dressed on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in camouflage uniform again. He had a rifle, a pistol, and I do not know what else. I think he had a cap somewhere or dark glasses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you able to describe the cap in any way, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A red beret I think he had stuck up here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know approximately the date that this occurred when you saw him on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was 8th June 1992, I am not sure, but I think that was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see Dule Tadic on an occasion after that not in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What were the circumstances when you saw Dule Tadic on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I had to go to Prijedor SUP every day to get a permit to move about, to get a pass.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you with anyone on this occasion that you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were my sons, and a lady neighbour of mine, Beska Kesic, that is, Mandic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How far were you from Dule Tadic when you saw him on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were standing in that column and he and Siha (sic) Adil were standing in a group and talking in front of the SUP building.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You say Siha and Adil, Siha and Adil who? What is their other name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims, Nasiha and Adil, and Adil Jakupovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you happen to see how Tadic was dressed on this occasion, Dule Tadic was dressed on this occasion, when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that occasion he was in civilian clothes, not in a uniform. That was the only time I saw him in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What date was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could have been mid June, perhaps latter half, the beginning of the latter half of June.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see him on any other occasions after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Prijedor, do you mean, I saw?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am sorry, yes, in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you see him on occasions after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only in the SUP in passing, Stenko, him, Cigo, Brdar, Sujica, Goran -- all those policemen I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: These are all other policemen that you knew. Were they Serbian policemen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The SUP is the police station, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On these other occasions when you saw him in and about the SUP building with these Serbian police officers, how was he dressed on those occasions, can you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When he was wearing invariably the camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: All of these occasions were in Prijedor city itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you look around the courtroom for me and see if you can see Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you point to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He never was so smartly dressed like this. Shame on you! Yes, in the middle between the two policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: During the time that you lived in and around Kozarac and the opstina Prijedor area, did you ever come across or -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The record will reflect that the witness has identified the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Niemann. MR. NIEMANN (To the witness): Did you on any occasion ever see or meet anyone or know of anyone who looked similar to Dule Tadic or who was occasionally mistaken for Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, he did not have a twin brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was there anyone other than a brother that may have been similar to him that you knew of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have no further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Mrs. Klipic, the first matter I want to talk to you about is when the attack took place on Kozarac. You have referred to the day that that occurred and you with your friends took shelter in a building in Kozarac, not at your home, but further up Marsala Tita Street, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was at a friend's house on Marsala Tita Street, but I am not sure what that street that leads towards the hospital is called. I was in the house of Hamid Najic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It seems to have been in the area near the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whilst you were in that house, there were shells falling on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And also in that area where you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I do not know if you can help us, but was the building that you were sheltering in, was that hit by a shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not the house, but the store, Nafik store, and that store was hit by a shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In fact, the position you showed us yesterday on the map that we had was very close to where Dule Tadic used to live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think it was a third or fourth house behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you went from the house where you were sheltering and went on to the street and turned the corner, you would be very close to where Dule Tadic's cafe and bar and the house was where his family lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Having sheltered there, you then decided with others to move out of Kozarac and to go into the woodland behind the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You took shelter in a summer house and that happened to be owned by someone you knew called Adil Jakupovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This move from the house where you had sheltered in in Kozarac, was that on the second day of the attack on the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Monday 25th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So, having spent the night in the town of Kozarac, the next day you decided with others that it was best to leave that town and move for refuge elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were there a large number of other people who had also taken that decision to leave Kozarac and take shelter up in the woods behind the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Like you, were they also sheltering in whatever places they could find?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told us that it would have been the third day that you then decided to leave that area and to go down to Kozarac, and that you were transported on a tractor with a trailer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, not the third day but the fourth day. Actually, the third day, the third day from the time when we went to the woods and the fourth day from the time of the attack, the Wednesday, 27th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That explains it. Were others also like you moving out of this area where they had taken refuge and going back down from the hills into Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on Tuesday afternoon we came down into Vidovici, a Serbian village, that had eight or nine houses, I am not sure how many, and that was not shelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know if others had left the woodland before you made that decision to come down to Kozarac, whether others had, in fact, moved down from those places of refuge earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, many columns left on Tuesday, meaning 26th, a lot of people surrendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you left on the third day it would have been in the woods, but the fourth day after the attack, had most of the people left the woodland then, were you amongst the last people or were there still many other people taking shelter up there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think we were the largest column, and I think the last one. I think that people were joining us from all over. There were a lot of people and there was a large column.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So was it in the village of Vidovici that you got the lift in the tractor with the trailer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you moved from Vidovici did you move down to the centre of Kozarac or did you go to another part of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, into the centre of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The route that you took, if you are able to help us, if we have Defence Exhibit 12 which is the blow-up of the map and perhaps if that could be put before the witness on the overhead projector? Is it more convenient for you, madam, to have it in front of you rather than leaning over to the projector? I do not know if the court would object if it was in front of her. I know your Honours have a copy of the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if it could be put in front of you and you will not have difficulty in orientating yourself. If you see the top right-hand corner, can you see "VIDOV"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is where the village of Vidovici is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you see on the left side of the map the word "Kozarac"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you see the triangle part which is at the end of Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean here?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I can see you are pointing with the stick. I can see where you are from where I am standing. Yes. Do you recognise Marsala Tita Street on this map? Going down to the triangle at the end of Kozarac, madam?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This around here is Kalate. I think that this is the main street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. In fact, we can see what you are doing if we put on the video monitor. Thank you very much. Now perhaps if you can tell us, and if the court video is able to do it again, put your finger in the area of Vidovici on the map and tell us the route that you went on from Vidovici down to Kozarac? Use your finger, madam, if it is easier than using the pointer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mutnik, I think I went here, then we went here, and then we came down Marsala Tita. We went Vidovici, Brdjani and then down here, this here, Arfagici, and that is not where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We now have the picture we wanted.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is up to you, Mr. Kay. If you wish the witness to use the overhead projector, she may; it is up to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we will go back to that. I appreciate yesterday she was having difficulty, your Honour. (To the witness): Perhaps if we can put it back -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not good in geography.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It does not matter. We might be able to find the route that you went on. Perhaps if we can put that map on the overhead projector, Mr. Bos, and we will try again? Perhaps you would like to move your chair closer to it, madam, it might assist you. The microphone will put up your voice nearer the projector.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mrs. Klipic, move towards that way a little bit and pull your microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you see there, Vidovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you able to trace with that pointer the route that you took from Vidovici down to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was perhaps this road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then we went here, this way, and then this way, and then we came to Mutnik mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then we came, I think, this down here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is toward Hrnici, this is towards Prijedor and this around Kalate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps if we can just stop there? You can tell me what time it was that you left Vidovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think around noon or 1 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember at all how long it took you to get down to Mutnik mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depends who had what kind of an appetite and how we came through here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember what time of day it was that you arrived there on the tractor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Brdjani, in Brdjani or Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, at the Mutnik mosque.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember. I think it was, as I said, we walked for half an hour and then we would stop and then we went for half an hour, then we would stop for 10 minutes, 20 minutes and then continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you able to tell me at all the numbers of people who were moving with you on this route?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Many. It was a very long column with tractors, cars, some people walked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you in the middle of the column or at the head of the column or at the back of the column? Are you able to tell us whereabouts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I was among the first behind. I am not sure exactly where my tractor was, but maybe first or second or third.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you moved from Mutnik mosque, you went down Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You went down to the triangle at the end of that street, the green triangle near the school in Kozarac, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you able to tell me about what time of day that was that you got there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have a watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it in the afternoon or evening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you able to say for how long you had been travelling from Vidovici, how long did it take you to get down there near the school in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will say again I do not know. In that fear, in all that crying, it is hard to tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You eventually went to Kozarusa, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you able by looking at the map we have had in the courtroom that you have just looked at, Defence Exhibit 12, to tell us which road you would have taken in Kozarac that took you to Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think this here. (Indicated).

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We cannot see where you are pointing and Mr. Bos will help you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the main street. It goes towards Krkici. These are Krkici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is probably not the direction of Kozarusa, is it, down there from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Krkici?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let me see if I put another map before you, it might make it easier. If we have map 79, if it can be put with Kozarac in the centre and perhaps blown up. That is what we need. Can you see that map now, madam? Can you see where Kozarac is? Can you see two roads, one with a "4" on it? Would that be the new road that would take you to Banja Luka or Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you see that? Your house was quite near that new road, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps looking at this map now you might be able to tell us where exactly your house was, that might help you? Are you able to point to that by looking at that map? Perhaps if you could keep your finger on the map as to where your house would be near the new ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you, either up here or down here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: OK. Can you see there "Kozarusa"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw it somewhere, I cannot find it now. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is very close to Kozarac, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is the place that you went to on your trailer and with the column of people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you can tell us, are you able to, by looking at this map, which direction you took on that trailer that took you to Kozarusa? Are you able to point to which road by looking at this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think this is the main road, Kozarac, Kozarusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that the road you took, the one that you are moving the pointer along at the moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is an old road and a new road. There is an upper Kozarusa -- Donja Kozarusa and Gornja Kozarusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. All I am trying to locate is where exactly you went to on your trailer when you told us that you went near a pub and the column of people stopped and were directed to various parts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you able to point by looking at this plan where on the map that place would be where you came to stop? Was it above the new highway or below the new highway? Was it near the old road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was by the new road and below the new road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That is probably all I need to direct you with in relation to that map for the moment. So you moved from Kozarac. You went to Kozarusa, and the column ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- came to a halt in Kozarusa, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The road that you took from Kozarac took you along the new highway which would take you to Prijedor; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So, leaving Kozarac you would have passed the old sawmill, would you? Would that have been one of the places you would have passed on your way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There turned right on to the new highway, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, can you remember what time it was that you arrived at Kozarusa and the column came to a halt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it could have been around 3.00 or 4 o'clock. It was still hot, warm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At this stage had more people joined your column that had initially moved from Vidovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts in the column were you when it arrived at Kozarusa? Were you still near the front or in a different part of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, still.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it right that more people had, in fact, joined that column as you progressed and made your way to Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that the column was larger and larger in the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told the court yesterday that whilst you were on the road that you saw a VW Golf police car that had been driven by Brane Bolta?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You said that Dusko Tadic was in that car with a man called Goran Borovnica and someone else whom you could not see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you saw that car, in which part of your journey did the car come near you? Whereabouts exactly had you travelled to at that stage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I was around the Bajina tavern.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The Bajina tavern is whereabouts? Is that in Kozarac or near the new highway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, by the new highway, close to Susici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have some further maps here to put before the court which decrease in scale from Defence Exhibit 12, your Honour, but they might be helpful. Your Honour, I put before the court a map now of a slightly different scale from the one that has been previously used which I tender as Defence Exhibit 13.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You are not going to have this witness identify it? I presume there will be no objection and that the Prosecution will stipulate with respect to this map, is there a problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. This is Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 13 Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 13 Defence. It will be admitted. It is a map of?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The Kozarac region again.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we put it on to the overhead projector? Again madam -- perhaps if we can have that on the video screen slightly smaller, more area shown or move it, thank you -- are you able to see Susici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Susici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you can indicate that on the plan that we have on the overhead projector?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Susici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Can you see the new highway below Susici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is the new highway is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Susici, Huskici, depending on how you mark them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you able to show us on this plan where that tavern was that you say you saw the car containing Dule Tadic and Brane Bolta, where it would be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could be around here, between Susici and probably close to Kozarac, about a kilometre from Kozarac, towards Susici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How far from where the column eventually stopped, as you said, Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think about two kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That would be going the other direction from Kozarac, would it not, madam?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At this stage the highway would have been full of many vehicles and people, all moving in the same direction that you were going, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We were moving in one direction and Serbs were moving in another direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say "Serbs were moving in another direction", what was the amount of traffic then that was going in the opposite direction to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a small traffic because the road was not large, and they were mostly walking and driving in cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say "Serbs were going in the opposite direction", what kind of Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Armed, dressed, all kinds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was the traffic in the road divided then into two columns, one going one way and the other traffic going the other way, so that the highway was divided as it would usually be in two sections?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): The area of the tavern where you saw Brane Bolta in a Golf car with Dusko Tadic and others was how far from the place in Kozarusa where eventually your column stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two-and-a-half, I believe, about two-and-a-half kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How long did it take you to travel that distance to stop the column in Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Had we been moving normally, that is 60 to 70, then it would have taken us about 10 minutes, but as it was it lasted longer. The column stopped often. I do not know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you can tell me then how much longer it took?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I should say about one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you saw the car containing Brane Bolta, it was travelling in the opposite direction which would be in the direction of Kozarac and Banja Luka, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you arrived in Kozarusa the column stopped at what point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By Zika's tavern in Kozarusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that in the centre of Kozarusa or by the new highway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By the new highway, at the bus station across the street from Zika's tavern.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When your column stopped there, were there other Muslim people or Croat, others who had been moved away from their homes, who were already there -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a small group, but that was when they started separating men from 16 to 65 years of age, that is, in front of Zika's tavern and we, women and children, remained on our tractors, buses, cars or whatever it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you arrived near Zika's tavern, how soon was it before you were separated and put in one direction for Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, until all the men were separated and until they had gone through all our bags.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So when you arrived at the bus station near Zika's tavern, had any of this procedure of separating people already started, or did it start when you arrived with your column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The separation began, I guess, and then others told me that the separation of men began in Kozarac already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But when you arrived there, there was only a few people at that stage, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was quite a number of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say "quite a number of people", who do you mean? Who were these people? Can you identify them in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were separating were Serbs and those who were separated from columns were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The Serbs who were separating people when you arrived, who were they? Can you identify them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were many. There were many I know and many more that I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Which ones did you know who were doing the separating when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Milos Preradovic, Rade Strika, Dule Tadic, Goran Borovnica, Tomo Stojakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you must have been very surprised to see Dule Tadic there because you had only seen him not long ago in a motor car driving in the opposite direction away from Kozarusa in the direction of Banja Luka or Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but he was in a car and one hour and a half, that was roughly how long we were there. I mean, it was easy to return.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have asked you about the times that things had taken on this journey to Kozarusa. You told us that the time from the area near the tavern where you saw Dusko Tadic in a motor car to the time that it took you to stop at the tavern near the bus station in Kozarusa was about an hour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An hour, an hour and a half. I am telling you, I did not have a watch and I was not interested in time. I wanted to know where people were going and what was going to happen to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you seen the car, the VW Golf, that you say you saw Mr. Tadic in driving past you, overtaking you on the way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That he came back or went in the direction of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On your way to Kozarusa, you say you saw Dusko Tadic in a motor car driving in the opposite direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. And after some time I saw him again in front of Kozarusa -- in front of Zika's tavern.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that the car was driving slowly, it could not drive fast because of the people on the highway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And he was going in the opposite direction to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were near the head of a long column of people ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- who were proceeding in this long chain which had started in Vidovici, through Kozarac and was making its way to Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told us that people were joining this column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And that on the way the car driving slowly in the opposite direction containing Dusko Tadic passed you and yet, you say, when you arrived in Kozarusa and people were being separated --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- Milos Preradovic, Goran Borovnica ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- that they were there in Kozarusa when you had seen them going in the opposite direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So they came back by car, they were in a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So they would have to have driven through the long column of people to get ahead of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did not obey any traffic rules; they used the same side again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you were very interested in blue police motor cars; as you have told us on many occasions, you were interested to observe who was in those cars because of the connection with your husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You would have noticed a blue police motor car threading its way slowly through a column of people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had many police cars, and very -- and very many Mercedes in Kozarac and that day they used them more than ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you did not see this car overtake you in that time it took you to get from the place on the new highway where you say you saw the car containing Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see him return. I saw him right before Kozarusa after some uncertain time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But when you arrive in Kozarusa he is part of this group of Serbs who are separating people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As to how he got back there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know -- ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am asking you, madam. Perhaps you would like to look at a statement that you made on 20th October 1995. What I seek to put before the witness is a translation of the English statement, as it would have been, into Serbo-Croat which has been provided to us by the Registry.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have any objection, Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have not seen the statement at this stage, your Honour, so I need to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I will provide it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That will be marked as -- what number are we at?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 14A, perhaps. Here is a copy for Mr. Niemann. (To the witness): Do you remember giving a statement on 20th October 1995 to someone called Thomas Ackheim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: With an interpreter called Nevenka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You gave a statement which was translated from Serbo-Croat into English, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After you had given that statement, you had it read back to you in your own language by Nevenka, and she told you that it was a statement in your language that was true to the best of your knowledge and recollection, is that right? Do you remember that, and that it was for the War ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- the International Criminal Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you recollect she asked you to sign an acknowledgment of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
