utterances.text: Perhaps you would like to look at this document here and just confirm that that is your signature? (Document handed to the witness). Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you look at the other page, you have signed the other pages before it as well, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps as that is the English version that can be returned to me, Mr. Usher. I would like you just to look at the first page of that statement that I have given to you in your own language. Can you confirm that there is no mention in that statement about seeing Dusko Tadic in a Golf motor car on 27th May on your way to Kozarusa, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did not, I had forgotten that. I can go on telling you about everything that happened to me for another six hours until 28th June in Prijedor. I want the truth. Where are those people? I do not know whether Dule killed them, but he must know the truth where these people are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were being questioned specifically about Dule Tadic, were you not, that is why the investigator spoke to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I may have forgotten that. I can give you as many statements as you want, but I do not think that only all those statements of mine are that important.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your statement was not really about everything else that happened to you; it was concentrating upon Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were aware, were you not, of the allegation against Mr. Tadic, that he killed your brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I had heard that but it was not Dule alone. There are thousands of them like Dule.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What I am suggesting to you is that you have made up this account that you saw Dule Tadic on 27th May in a Golf motor car on the highway and in Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not true. I said the truth. I know whom I saw where. I would be happy if I were lying to you and if my family were alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What I would like to ask you about now is some of that detail concerning the separation of people in Kozarusa. Before I do that, I would like you to just look at your statement in your own language and the paragraph dealing with 27th May 1992 so that you can see what you said last year. That is on that first page you have just looked at.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In that statement is it right that you say that he was dividing the people, deciding who should be sent to Omarska, Keraterm and Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he, Milos and all the others listed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But in this statement you say that he was deciding, "I heard him decide who to be sent to Omarska, Keraterm and Trnopolje".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were loudly consulting: "What are we going to do with this one? Where are we going to send that one?" I did not know at that time; later on I heard they were taking them to Omarska and Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If I can remind you of what you told the court yesterday and that was that Dusko Tadic was asking: "Where do I take them?" You were asked: "Who did he ask?" and you told the court: "Milos Preradovic".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Strika, Bolta, they were all there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But that is very different, is it not, from on one account you say Dusko Tadic deciding who was going to be separated, who was going to go where, and what you said in court yesterday which was that he was asking where to send people; he was being told where to send people? Do you appreciate the difference?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know how you would feel after four years, or I do not know how long, without your family, if anybody asked you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Because what I am suggesting to you is that you are making up this account against ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- Mr. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is what you think, but we think what we know and what we saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That you are inventing a role for him in what took place in the Kozarac region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would be very happy to invent that and have my family alive. I want the truth, where my brothers, my husband and my relatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say you saw Mr. Tadic on that day of 27th May, can you describe his appearance, what he looked like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarusa that day, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a camouflage uniform, he was slightly unkempt, not really, but he was unshaven. He did not have a beard but he was unshaven.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In this statement that I have just put before you, if you would like to look at the paragraph below that of 27th May, there are two lines, do you not say he was clean shaven?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. He had no time to be clean shaven. Clean shaven he was when I last saw him in Kozarac. He was then clean shaven. I do not know how to explain it. Then he did not have a beard, but he looked like someone who had not shaved for two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you will agree with me, though, will you not, that in this statement here you are quite specific; you say he was, to the best of your recollection, clean shaven? Is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know really what to tell you. You are a professional and I am not. I am telling the truth and you can think what you like. His beard and his continence were of no interest to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you were asked to think about these matters because in the paragraph before when you say what happened on 21st May 1992 -- perhaps you would like to look at that short paragraph before 27th May in your statement in your language? Perhaps you would like to do that, the one before, the paragraph before 27th May. It is on the first page. It starts: "On 21st May 1992 ..." Well, it is a matter for you whether you want to look at that statement or not, but in there you said that he had a, had a few days growth but not a beard before the attack? So you were thinking about these matters, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What did I say?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were thinking about these matters. You were trying to remember what he looked like because you described him as not having a few days growth, but not a beard, in a few days before the attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He looked unkempt, just a little, some growth. He has a very strong beard and he does not shave for a day or two and, at any rate, I said I was not interested in his beard. I was not interested as a man. As a man I met him passing in Kozarac on that particular day. Unfortunately I had no photographic camera or anything to take a shot of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say he was in a camouflage uniform, did you notice anything unusual about the uniform that you say he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what you think. A camouflage uniform, like any camouflage uniform, he had an automatic rifle and a pistol and a belt and God knows what else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like to now move to Trnopolje which is where you were sent from Kozarusa, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you arrive in Trnopolje on 27th May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How many days did you stay in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ten or 12, I do not know exactly. I went in 27th and on the 8th I left to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember the date that you left and went to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot exactly, but I think I did say 8th or 10th. My children had contracted dysentery and I had to take them urgently to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you staying in the camp in Trnopolje which was where the cinema was and other buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was in the third house from the camp and that was also guarded by the army. It was Alija Grdan's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So you were outside what I would otherwise call the centre of the camp, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I went to the centre, to the camp every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it two children you had with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, two sons, two and a half and four and a half years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did one or both of them contract dysentery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, both. They had lost liquid. They both had diarrhoea. They could not walk. So I left them with a colleague of mine. I went down to the doctor to tell me if he had something. They told me they had nothing. So I took my children to take the bus and Pero gave me permission to go to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The reason you were going to Prijedor was presumably to go to the Prijedor hospital to get some treatment, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I went to the medical centre in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How many occasions did you leave Trnopolje in that way to go to the Prijedor medical centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was in Trnopolje until the day, all the time until the 8th or the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So when you leave to go to Prijedor to the medical centre with your children, is that the day that you stop your confinement in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So you move from Trnopolje on that day. Did you have any accommodation arranged for you in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I with was with my husband's brother, that is his wife in Donja Puharska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did someone give you permission to leave Trnopolje so that you could then go and live in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Presumably gave you documents that supported that, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they gave me a certificate so that I could go from Trnopolje to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So this occasion when you go to the Prijedor medical centre, is the day that you do not return to Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and I also went from Prijedor to Trnopolje when I heard that my father-in-law was killed, and that was June, towards the end of it, I do not know when, but towards the end of it, late June.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So there was another occasion when you were able to leave Prijedor to visit Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and I again had to obtain a document from the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you did not have to stay in Trnopolje; you were able after that to return to Prijedor, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I returned to Prijedor and once again I went to fetch my mother-in-law to Duracci, also to obtain paper and bring her back to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Looking at the time, as I wish to now, that you were actually in the village of Trnopolje, were you staying with people who had a house there or were you just put into a house that belonged to other people? Perhaps you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was with those people. There was the landlord Adil and there were very many other neighbours of ours from Kamicani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have told the court this morning that on two occasions whilst you were at Trnopolje you saw Dusko Tadic not in the camp but in the village of Trnopolje itself, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him once, I have already said that, when I went to Trnjani from the camp to my relatives to get my children.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How soon after you had been in the camp do you say that the first occasion was that you saw Dusko Tadic in the area of Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the area around Trnopolje I saw Dule several days later, after five or six days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was he on his own or with others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First I saw him, the first time I think, maybe the second, the first time I saw him coming from Prijedor towards Trnopolje. I was going towards Trnjani with my children so that they could have a bath and have a meal with my relative, and I saw him with Bolta, I do not know if it was a Golf, in any case, it was a police car and they were going towards Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If I can just look at what you have told us there. Would it be then the first occasion you were on your way somewhere so that your children could have a bath in another house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts was the house that you were taking them to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was at Ilijaz Trnjanin's house, my relative. He is about one and a half kilometres from Trnopolje towards Duracci below the road towards Garevci, the lower road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps we can look at Exhibit 79 and a place a copy before the witness on the overhead projector. If you would like to look at this map, Mrs. Klipic, and if the screen can come back a bit and the map moved up to include part of the lake. Just stop there. Thank you. We do not see the town name Trnopolje on this map because it is Kozarac Station that has been named. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have been told that that is the area of Trnopolje around Kozarac Station. Is that something that you would agree with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it used to be called, the railway station used to be called Kozarac Railway Station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you able to see on there the place where you were going with your children to the house of your relative so that they could have a bath?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see Trnjani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you can indicate it with the stick on the map which is on the overhead projector? I think you will find Trnjani is the other direction there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Trnjani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you recognise the place where their house would be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. (Indicated). I think that it is a little bit in here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. When you saw Dusko Tadic with Brane Bolta in a vehicle, whereabouts was that vehicle when you were walking from Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The car was going from Prijedor and I was going towards Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So it was somewhere on that road, was it, that we can see marked on ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I cannot remember exactly what exactly, what place exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You walked on the road rather than walking on any other paths or any our route?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we walked on the road, on the side of the road because there is no sidewalk; just asphalt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did the car stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It drove past. Did you say anything to the car or gesture to it in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I looked, you know, Bolta and of course you wonder what is he going to ask you. Although we always met in Prijedor I would always ask him about people, but at that time he just passed by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The car was going in the opposite direction or the same direction as you were walking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Opposite direction, from Prijedor towards Trnopolje, and I was going from Trnopolje towards Prijedor which means towards Trnjani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again this was a blue police car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think. I am not sure exactly what car, but it was a police car. I noticed that the best.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was there any other traffic on the road at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was the car driving at an ordinary speed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, normal. It was not going too fast because the road had pot holes in there. It was asphalt but it had pot holes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The other occasion at Trnopolje when you say you saw Dusko Tadic, was that in the camp itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was outside of the camp. There was a tavern Huskina's tavern across from the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was he with anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was with Goran Babic, Zoka from the gas station, Goran the taxi driver. There were many familiar faces but I cannot remember the names of all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was this Goran the taxi driver who was married to a Muslim woman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Otherwise called Zoran, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zoran, Goran, Zoran, I am not sure. I just know that he was married to Amina and he had three children and he was a taxi driver. I am not exactly sure about his name and I do not know even know his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know if his wife or children were in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: They were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know what he was doing there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. Everybody was standing there. I really did not see who was doing what but I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you sure that this was Goran or Zoran who had a relative who was a Muslim in the camp, or could it have been someone else other than he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was Goran. Zoka from the gas station was there. Goran, Zoran, there are many of those people and I always have them mixed up, but I know he had three children with Amina. That Zoka from the gas station, I knew him the best and I saw him and Goran Babic, policemen who worked until Saturday evening in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were there a large number of policemen or guards or military people around this area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were. There was a group of people, I do not know how many, in there. As I am saying to you, I was not really counting. I never even knew I would be free eventually and where would I live.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did people come to the camp who had relatives in there, perhaps wives or other members of their family, to try to get them released from the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you get anyone from your family out of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Out of Trnopolje? Were you able to have someone released to you from the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I had my mother-in-law. I fetched them at the Duracci village and I got her there and I took her to Puharska. She was not in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was the place where your mother-in-law placed near Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that place is called Duracci. I do not know how many kilometres it is from Trnopolje, perhaps 3 or 4 in the direction of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did people used to come to Trnopolje camp whilst you were there and arrive and look for relatives or friends whom they believed to be in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know who got whom out. I know that I saw several Muslims in Prijedor who were not in the camp and who got them out of there, and it was probably friends, just like, for example, I think I heard that Dule took out Adil and Nasiha Jakupovic and in Prijedor I saw Hamdija Tadic he had his two sons and his brother-in-law and a son.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So you think that Dule Tadic was able to get out of Trnopolje a Muslim friend of his?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know where he got him out, whether from the column or Trnopolje, I am not sure. I know they were with us in Kozarusa. Nasiha and Adil were with us. We were in the column together all the time, but whether it was Dule, as I say, I do not know who took them out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I just thought you said that Adil Jakupovic was in the building where you were in the Trnopolje, in the house where you were staying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in Trnopolje. In Kozarac in the shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What I suggest to you is that you did not see him twice in the region of Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Inaudible).

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you may have seen him once in the time that you were there and, indeed, with a man looking for somebody at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Who do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Jovo Samovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jovo Samovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never heard of him, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But what you can tell us from your account is that on one occasion you saw him there was a man with him who was married to a Muslim woman who had three children who was Goran or Zoran?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have also told the court that you saw Mr. Tadic in Prijedor later on in June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And he was dressed in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You say it was in front of the SUP building, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You in fact mention a Muslim man Adil Jakupovic as being with him as well as his wife, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In the statement that you gave last year, if you can just turn to the second page of it, all I want to do is help you with a date. You actually name a date, do you not, as being 15th June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I saw Adil and Siha, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. You say you saw Mr. Tadic on that day, 15th June, in civilian clothes in Prijedor, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him, but whether it was exactly that date, I said that approximately. I cannot really remember the date exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right, but for what it is worth on this occasion you actually said that date, 15th June, which must have seemed right to you or about right when you gave it, do you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, approximately. I roughly remember, I am not exactly sure. I said I saw him in the morning. I remember it was early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you saw him with Adil Jakupovic, could it in fact have been in front of the Hotel Balkan in Prijedor rather than at the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It was in front of the SUP building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was there any particular reason why you should remember where they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because there were a lot of us who had, who needed every day those same authorisations which would enable us to move through Prijedor every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember what day of the week it would have been when you say him? Is there any particular reason why a day of the week would have been of interest to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really do not know. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Niemann, do you have any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit 14 was not offered. I do not know whether you want to offer the whole statement or whether you just want it offered for identification purposes only to use in questioning?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Only for identification purposes for use in questioning, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Very good. Mr. Niemann, you referred to a list of policemen that the witness had prepared, a list of missing policemen or policemen who she thought were missing. You remember there was much dialogue between you two attorneys about it and you did not offer it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Did you intend to offer it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there anything else from either counsel? No. Is there any objection to Mrs. Klipic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, there is not, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mrs. Klipic you are excused. Thank you for coming to testify. You are excused. You may leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. I want the truth to come out.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may leave. (The witness withdrew).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for lunch then until 2.30.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: (Luncheon Adjournment).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I apologise to the lawyers and to Mr. Tadic for the Trial Chamber being almost 10 minutes late. We have been rather careful with the time and encouraged the parties to be here and ready and sometimes we have come in and you have not been here, so we apologise to you. We were meeting on three other matters and we spent our lunch hour eating whatever we were eating and working, so I apologise. We will make it up somehow -- we will make up the time, that is! So, where are we? Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am sorry. Is it on the correct channel? All I had said, Mr. Tadic, is that I apologise for the Judges coming in late, nine minutes late. The reason we were late is that we were meeting to discuss three or four other matters and so we spent our lunch hour doing that, but I do apologise because we wanted to set a standard of being on time. Mr. Tieger, would you call your next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. The Prosecution's next witness is Nihad Seferovic. MR. NIHAD SEFEROVIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Seferovic, would you please take that oath?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare -- a solemn declaration. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Mr. Tieger, you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, will you state your name please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nihad Seferovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Seferovic, where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What is your nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you grow up in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On what street in Kozarac did you grow up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Marsala Tita Street, No. 38.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was your occupation before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a carpenter in the sawmill. I was engaged in timber processing at the sawmill. I processed timber at the sawmill.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you serve in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were your duties as a soldier with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For six months I was in infantry and then I was in a work department.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what year were you born, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In the 1970s and the beginning of the 1980s did you work frequently outside of Kozarac in parts of Europe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During that time did you return to Kozarac as often as you could?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, especially for weekends.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In the 1980s, around 1984 or so, did you return to Kozarac for good to stay in work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You did not leave until the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you build a home for yourself in the area of your parents' home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, 70 metres, up to 70 metres from the road, from the old house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to show you a video tape and ask if you will identify homes and businesses as you see them on the video. It may be moving fast, and I also would like you, if you can, to point out the area of your home that you can see on the video. So if we could have Exhibit 195 shown, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Krkici, a pastry shop, pastry shop, butchers, bakery, "Restaurant".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that an actual restaurant or a building called "Restaurant"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A building called "Restaurant".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. Now can we proceed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule's neighbour, Dule's coffee bar house, family house, neighbour's house, then shopping, a road to hospital, neighbour's house, another one, another one, another one. Here a shop ought to be, fifth, sixth -- stop, this is my house. If you can get it back slightly to the left?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Forwards, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Stop here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: OK. Just a little bit forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just a tiny bit forward, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, my house, my old house, and the new one cannot be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we proceed, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Ismet Fazlic's, Alija Redic's, the Fire Brigade, old Municipal Hall, Edam Susic's, post office, cinema, beyond the cinema, the road to the old town, a shop, a shop, summer garden, Hamza Tadic's house, old post office, a summer garden, a road to the old town, a shop, supermarket, Vakuf seat, shops, Mezarluk, which is cemeteries, a road to the old town and surrounding villages, the mosque, cemeteries in front, mosque, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, you pointed out the house and cafe of Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That appeared to be fewer than 10 houses away from your house, as you pointed it out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not 10, eight or nine, I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know Dule Tadic when you were growing up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you play together as children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What name did you know him by as a child?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Dule", "Dusko", "Dusan".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you closer in age to his older brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mladen and Ljubo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you also know Dule Tadic's parents' names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was his father's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Late Ostoja.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: His mother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Staka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you continue to know Dule Tadic as you grew up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until I found a job -- I mean, I have always worked outside but there was, "Hello, how are you?" since we were children. When I began to work, then it would be: "Hello, what's new? How are you?" and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you returned to Kozarac to stay, did you see Dule Tadic frequently and chat with him often?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not so often, but we talked.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know who his wife was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What is her name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mira.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know how many children he had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they had two children, I think, both girls.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When Dule Tadic built his cafe did you participate in that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that because you were a professional carpenter and you were paid?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not know how it got there. I think we were first building the foundations and then we went upward to the attic, and then I went on working at Mladen's and at Dule's, from the foundations to the finishing of the roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you work on the inside of the cafe as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was Mladen making an addition to the home at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was not building a house but he was making some additions to his house. I do not know, I mean, whatever it was, a house again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did other people, other neighbours, local people from the area, help in the building of the cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was all of that assistance because these people were paid or was part of it a reflection of a local custom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is a custom when some major work has to be done, and then acquaintances come and, yes, it was all agreed upon, but when there is a major thing going on, then we helped with the foundations, with the ground floor and the roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is there a word for that custom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, "gajret", we call it "gajret".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What does "gajret" mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not hear what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does "gajret" have a translation? Does the word "gajret" have a translation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I have not heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. It just refers to that custom of helping neighbours out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did local Muslims participate in the building of Dule Tadic's cafe, according to the custom of gajret?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, my brother was there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Over the years of knowing Dule Tadic since the time he was a child and you were a child, and associating with each other as adults, did you come to know his appearance quite well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was his build? Was he a thin man, a strong man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was quite solid, I should say -- he still is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he sometimes have a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes, not always, sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So sometimes he did and sometimes he did not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know who some of his friends or acquaintances were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not he was friendly with Emir Karabasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they were friends. They trained Karate together, practised Karate together, but later on, no, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As the time grew closer to the outbreak of conflict, the attack on Kozarac, did Dule Tadic begin to associate less with Muslims and more with Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know who he was associating with shortly before the time of the attack on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know Miso Radulovic and Vaso -- I do not know his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was Miso Radulovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a teacher in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was he a Muslim or a Serb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was Vaso?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vaso was a Montenegrin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know a man named Goran Borovnica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where was he from? Where did he live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know where he lived, but I do not know where his mother and father were from.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what town did he live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac, he lived above the "Restaurant".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know whether he and Dule Tadic knew each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see them in each other's presence or associating with each other often before the time of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he came often to Dule Tadic's cafe before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Seferovic, let me ask you a few questions about the period of time immediately before the attack on Kozarac, and by that I mean within just a few weeks before. Was it possible at that time for Muslims to travel outside Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were the roads blocked for Muslims both in the direction of Prijedor and in the direction of Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether or not anything had happened to the television programming by that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, all of the relays were taken away and we were forced to watch Serbian television.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were any of the important institutions in Kozarac being guarded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you remember which ones?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that the school was guarded, the church and several other institutions in Kozarac, supermarkets, and I do not remember what else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How many guards do you remember at each institution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up to two, up to three guards -- actually sawmill as well, I forget to mention that, factories around Kozarac. Of course, it was normal that they increased the number of guards, they increased it by two and, how should I say this, yes, there was a civilian protection. There were people, there were young men that had the SMB uniforms and, of course, they had weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there any checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, in major intersections.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Which nationalities were involved in this guarding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that all three nationalities, Serbs, Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall when the attack on Kozarac began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was 26th, I know it was a Sunday, but I do not remember exactly what date it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had the Serbian residents of Kozarac already left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but not all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not Dule Tadic was still in Kozarac when the attack began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you when the attack began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At work or at home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was Sunday so I did not work.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did you do when the attack started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I ran out into the road. A car came by, I sat into the car and I said "stop" and then I went into the hills, into Besici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you stop to change your clothes or to pack any belongings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. No, I just left. I was dressed in civilian clothes as usual.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you have a weapon with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you end up at the home of people you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did other Muslims from central Kozarac also flee to that part of the hills?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not all of them. There were several convoys.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you go back to Kozarac at any point to retrieve some belongings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I did go back later. In the evening I went back home. I had a lot of birds and I fed the birds. I took my back pack and I went back into the hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was the shelling still going on at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had most of the citizens of Kozarac fled from Kozarac by that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You indicated that the attack began on a Sunday. Do you remember what day of the week it was when people first started to surrender?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not remember at all what day it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was it within a -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that it was a very nice day in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was it within approximately three days after the shelling began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so. I do not remember because I went through a terrible catastrophe myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In any event, whatever day of the week it was or whatever the date was, did you go into Kozarac? Did you leave Besici and go into Kozarac on the first day that people began to surrender?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I was looking for my brother, for my family members, friends, relatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you first got into Kozarac what was happening? What did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, people were leaving. They did not know where they were going. I went to my brother's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On what street did your brother live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember the name of the street, but straight from the church towards the hospital and towards the main street. The road was going straight and then the hospital would be to the right and the main street to the left, from the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may at this time, perhaps we could have marked for identification a map which may assist the witness? That would be Exhibit 220. (To the witness): Mr. Seferovic, do you recognise this as depicting portions of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That is very obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 220 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May we have that placed on the elmo, please? (To the witness): First of all, Mr. Seferovic, can you point out where your house was located? If you could point on the map which is on the machine to your right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think here and here. (Indicated).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you point out the general area of Besici or the general direction of Besici to the extent it is possible on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that the bridge is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Seferovic, you will have to point on the document that is on that machine if we are going to be able to see it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the first bridge that you can take for Besici. This is the second bridge that you can take to go to Besici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you point out on this map where your brother's house was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicated) Here, somewhere here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That would be the street between the hospital and the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was your brother at his home when you got there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not find anyone at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After that, did you move to a point a little bit closer to the Prijedor/Banja Luka highway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I saw what was happening around the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could have this marked as Exhibit 221 for identification? It is an enlarged portion of the same map which was just introduced. (To the witness): Mr. Seferovic, can you recognise this as an enlarged portion of the same map you were just looking at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think it is just -- it just shows a wider area, yes, a larger one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender 221 for admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 221 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Mr. Seferovic, can you show us on this map where your brother's house was and the position you moved to after leaving your brother's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicated) I think here. This is where my brother's house, and I then went through the gardens, through the back yards and then I came to this house, the last house here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What is across the street from that spot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is a church yard and a church.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The area you were in where you stopped, what was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is -- in front of the house there are bushes and an orchard with flowers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we call up Z5-29, please? Mr. Seferovic, do you recognise what is shown in the photograph on the bottom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a church.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that the church which was across the street from the position you were in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First of all, before we do that, do you see the fence in front of the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In the picture at the upper left, can you see a continuation of that fence shown in that photograph? Perhaps we can have the upper left photograph enlarged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Would that be shown on the left side of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. One can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you see the orchard or garden where you were that day in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that the area depicted on the right side of the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on the right side of the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is the area immediately behind those hedges where the trees are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those are the plums, plum trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In this photograph we can also see a road that is the road on which the fence is. As we are looking at the photograph, that road leads toward where? I am talking about the road that the people in the picture are walking on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This road is leading to Krkici, to Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We can also see the bottom portion of a road which meets that road in the lower right-hand part of the picture. If we could return to Z5-29, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this road up here leads to the hospital, to the right, on the right side, and the road on the left is leading to the main street.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So the picture on the right is the road leading from the area of the church to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and the one on the left side towards -- is leading towards Marsala Tita Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So these two pictures show an intersection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we have the picture on the upper right blown up, please? Just to clarify, although everyone may already appreciate this fact, are those hedges to the left in this photograph then the same hedges that are shown in the picture we were looking at before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The hedges on the left, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So, you were on the other side, in the yard on the other side of those hedges then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was by the plum trees because it was summer or spring time, it was spring time, so the trees were covered with leaves, and in this picture everything, the trees are naked so it all looks like it is all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Could we return to Z5-29 once more? So when you arrived in the yard which is most clearly shown in the photograph on the upper left, were you able to see across the street to what was happening by the Serbian church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I could see clearly everything because I could move, I do not know in what diameter, but in front of the church there was police from Kozarac with their hands below their necks -- behind their necks. I think there were six. I do not quite remember. Out of those six I recognised four, Emir, Osman, Edin and Ekrem. In front were Dusko Tadic, Borovnica, Dule, and some other paramilitary soldiers. I am not quite sure who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You mentioned some names of Muslim police officers; you mentioned the name "Edin". Did you know his last name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Besic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You also mentioned the name "Ekrem". Did you know his last name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also Besic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You mentioned the name "Emir"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Karabasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You mentioned "Osman", did you know his last name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Osman was not from Kozarac. I just know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know his position with the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was a Commander of a police unit, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You also mentioned some paramilitary soldiers. Approximately how many paramilitary soldiers were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 15. I did not count them. I saw a larger group of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What nationality were those paramilitary soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Naturally Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, perhaps I can ask you to mark on Exhibit 221 the position the Muslim policemen were in and the position the Serbian paramilitary soldiers were in when you saw them? Your Honour, we can either do that with the document as it is or I can supply another copy of the same document.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, do you have any objection to the witness marking on Exhibit 221?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No problem at all.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Sir, does the straight line you have marked indicate the police officers or the Muslim police officers or the Serbian soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because they were standing in line.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I am sorry, the straight line is which, the policemen, the Muslim policemen or the Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Muslim policemen, not Serb army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The Serbian soldiers are indicated by the various dots between the church and the paths?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You were right across the street, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there also civilians in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a larger group passing by, and I paid attention to them just for a minute and then afterwards I concentrated my attention to the church and what was happening around it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you were watching, did the Serbian soldiers direct or control the movements of the civilians who were going by?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, no-one was allowed to look to the side. They were waving with arms, with weapons, and they were pointing their weapons towards the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How were the Serbian soldiers dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms, some may have been in SMB. I do not know. I did not pay attention to everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were the Serb soldiers armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did any of them have their weapons aimed at or trained at the Muslim policemen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It was -- the arms were always aimed at us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did any of the Serbian soldiers have any type of hats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did. Some had some caps, some did not. I do not remember. It was a beautiful day. I mean, it does not really matter. Most of them had caps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether any of them had arm bands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did around the arm, they had blue or white. I do not remember it all, but I think that, by and large, they had some white arm bands.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you continue to observe this scene for some period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Those paramilitaries provoked the civilians no end. At a certain point, Dule Tadic came, dragged Osman from the group, shouted, "Follow me", got him by his neck, and cut his throat and then stabbed him below that several times, I do not know how many times, and then he proceeded to Edin Besic, and with the same -- and he hit him in the same way as he did Osman; and this was followed by incredible fire, and I then ran away. I followed the same path and I cut through and ran to Besici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would like to move through that with you just a little bit slower, if I may? When you saw Dule Tadic approach Osman, exactly what did you see him do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He pulled him out quickly from that line up. I did not see the knife, only blood gushed, burst to all sides, and there were more stabs and then he moved over to Edin. I saw the same thing on Edin, and then terrible fire ensued to celebrate, I guess, I do not know why, and I retreated in despair.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you say "fire" do you mean gunfire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You say you retreated from the scene, where did you go? Did you go back to Besici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I went to Besici very, very slowly. I do not even know how I got there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you use the main streets or some other way of getting back to Besici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, there are many roads in Kozarac. All houses are wide open, wherever you enter, nobody. I mean, before the war anybody was welcome, all the houses were wide open, so that I could -- the last time I could go through without a welcome, I could go to Besici. You do not understand that. I used to the word to explain that I could slowly, slowly go through them to Besici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Within a few days did you return do Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I kept coming back to Kozarac because I had many birds, I felt the need to feed them. The last time, unfortunately, I was hit in the leg by a bullet, I do not know where from, was it a stray bullet or whether it was on purpose but I was fired all the time, non-stop around the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you were struck by that bullet did you manage to make your way back to Besici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I did manage to get back to Besici with the help of a stick, on a stick, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did you stay after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I stayed in that chestnut grove. There is a stream and the nature had dug it out, there was -- the rains had eroded it and they sort of excavated a shelter and I stayed there. I cannot remember anything, how long, because I was in terrible pain. I was all alone, and the only help was alcohol and my underwear, my under-shirts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you say "alcohol" do you mean alcohol to drink or alcohol for your wound?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not drink. I stopped drinking some seven or eight years ago, I do not remember, seven years ago, I believe. No, I used it to separate the wound from my clothes because it stuck to it. It was bleeding terribly and I had nothing else. I had to clean it somehow. The only thing I had, alcohol or plum brandy our Slivovitz.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you assisted by a friend or someone from Besici at the beginning of the time or for some period of time while you were in that hole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, a friend brought food, basics, some bread, for the first five, maybe six, days, I do not remember, and then he left and I never saw him again to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you finally leave the hole and attempt to go back to Kozarac in an effort to find your family or friends?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do not remember how many days I spent in the hole, but the pain was excruciating. I fainted several times and when the swelling receded I stood up. I somehow found superhuman strength to stand up, to pull myself up, with the help of that stick, and move and go and try to find my brother because I knew he had stayed in Kozarac, and -----

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I will proceed then. When you got to Kozarac, did you reach your brother or were you unable to do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I climbed down, I cut across the road, Besici, Mutnik, and I was going down to the old town. I was very thirsty, exhausted after that journey and I drank a lot of water. Since everything was overgrown, grass, plum trees were all bent down to the black earth, so I walked normally. I was not even trying to hide. When I stepped on to the road I heard a burst of fire, one and then two more, and they were all firing at me. I do not know what it was, but I was not hit and they captured me that night. The whole night with them, ill treatment. I do not know what they did. The wound was bleeding. I could not stop the bleeding. Rifle butts were hitting me from all sides. No, no, I do not remember. I do not remember almost anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did they take you after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I spent the night there and then in the morning two men came, battered me, two, "Ustasha". They tied my hands round their neck and hung me by the rail next to the small truck. For a while I knew, then I fainted. I was lying on the floor. I do not know how long they drove me, I do not remember and, yes, I got to the camp. Five, six of them got me and then threw me up as a basketball, head down against the ground. I all burst and then shoes in the jaw, I do not know, and after that I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The translation I received or what I heard was that you said there were two Ustasha who tied your hands; what did you mean by "Ustasha"? What nationality were these persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they called me "Ustasha". They were two Chetniks, those, the Serb paramilitary army, they called me "Ustasha" -- me who has never picked up a rifle except in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Which camp were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The camp Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I move on, can we tender Z5-29 as Exhibit 222?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Just a matter of clarification, that is the combined picture, not the blown up?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is the three photos, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If it is the combined picture of three of them, then it is fine. Then we understand what is tendered here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, it brings up a good point. I would like to tender the three photos individually so the court can have much clearer and make it easier for the court, than the print out which will eventually come from the three.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: But not the blow-ups?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. How do you want to label them? 222A, B, C or 222 jointly, maybe A, B, C so we will not lose them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is fine.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 222A, B and C will be admitted without objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What then is A, B and C?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I would say -- A will be -- I do not know, we will ask them to mark them. That is a good point, Mr. Wladimiroff. How would you like them marked, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would ask that we have some representation of the exhibit we were looking at before, so it could either be 222 and then A, B and C would be the individual photos.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. 222 will be the joint all three photos and then how will you label them individually?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could have the numbers back? I am sorry. I would label A49/9, 49/10 would be B and 1/27 would be C. So that would be 1/27 is the church at the bottom. That is why I put that as C. 49/9 and 49/10 are the left and right of the photos above. So, moving across, you have A on the left, B on the right and C on the bottom.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I understand that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. They are admitted. Thank you. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Mr. Seferovic, do you recognise the model in front of you as a representation of Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Perhaps you can show us into which part of Omarska you were taken after you arrived? We will do it one at a time. If you could show us, first, the building you were taken to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, here, I was brought here to this building for interrogation. (Indicated) I did not say anything. I could not say anything. Really, I was not conscious at all because of the beatings. They did not even interrogate me or beat me. They simply sent me to this big building. I do not remember when or how. I only know I came to the last room. I think -----

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you point first, sir, and then we will .....

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is where the room is here. (Indicated), here, the last room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. Your Honour, if we could remove the roofs, perhaps the witness would be able to show us the room he was in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there is no need. The roofs, these roofs kept us from -- kept us warm very well. We were right below the roof. We were right below this roof which was a tin roof. Do you know how a tin roof heats in the summer -- no, you do not have to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I ask you this when maybe you can describe where you were, were you on the ground floor or the upper floor of that large building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on the upper floor. There is a large staircase, a staircase, then they turn, then you turn. On the right-hand is the entrance to the big room, and to the left is the toilet and some cupboards. There was no room for a packet of cigarettes. That is how we were lying down. From the door to the last part, to the last, there was no room at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Within a short time after you arrived, did you see anyone in that same room whom you had seen at the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, almost all villagers from Kozarac, almost all my friends, neighbours, and then I was very, very surprised when I saw Emir Karabasic. I was very weak, exhausted. I was lying down. I could not move and people made room for me, accepted me in the camp. I do not know. That night passed. I think that Emir suffered a major battering. The next day three of us remained, myself, Emir Karabasic, Mujo Kolera, Kulenovic. The whole camp went out. I got up. I crawled to Emir and took out a cigarette. I had a slice of bread. We shared it, partook of it, and then I lit a cigarette and asked Emir: "Why are you shaking? Why do you have nightmares when you cannot get up properly?" He said: "They wanted to cut my throat but I survived". I told him about what happened before the church and he confirmed it. The folk were already entering the camp and the room and everybody had to sit in his place because none of the -- none of the camp inmates would give his room, and I moved away crawling and sat back in my place, disappointed, disenchanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was Emir Karabasic called out of the room within a few days of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next day, I believe, towards -- in the late afternoon he was called out, Jasko Hrnic, Enver Alic, Enver's father, I do not remember his name, but he was of an advanced age. He was in my room. He was called out to see what was in store for his son, whether he would survive.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you hear screams coming from the downstairs area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those were superhuman screams. I do not know whence the strength to these people to shout so much, to yell so loudly, and then all of a sudden everybody went silent, silence reigned everywhere, everybody kept silent for two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Emir Karabasic return to the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Never, no, not one of the three of them came back, nor did I see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During the time you were in Omarska were other prisoners called from the rooms and beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every day, every day they called out, regardless of who had done what or who had been what, what had been, the rich people, intelligentsia were killed and the poor people, of course, they were always suffer the worst.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not prisoners were beaten during interrogations? Could you see their conditions before they left for interrogation and when they came back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not have to speak. They never did. One could see it on them. They were all like your rope; only their faces were whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How often were you fed in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know if I can say that that was food. We were given one-eighth part of a loaf of bread. That was a slice of bread a day. It almost always, some left overs which had turned sour, rancid.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you beaten in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, I kept getting beaten. I was always the last one. I could not run because one went to eat, running, a group of 30 had to finish their meal in about half a minute to a minute and they would eat and I often stayed hungry. I would not get my meal. I would simply get my bread and go out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there prisoners who were called out to be beaten who did not return to their rooms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, every evening, every evening, every evening, they called people out and they never returned to the room. They only filled it up from other places in Kozarac and Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you transferred to Manjaca camp when the bulk of the prisoners were moved from Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. I was transferred to Manjaca. They read out lists for eight hours, and then when they would finally have so many -- they could never agree about the number of the prisoners on the lists -- then finally they told us: "Well, get on to the buses", so we got there and they were beating us with their rifle butts, with their boots and trampling on us. Then we started for Manjaca, I mean Omarska, when we boarded the buses to Manjaca. We arrived late, late in Manjaca. I did not have a watch. Nobody had a watch.
