They had taken them all from us -- jewellery, watches, they took off sneakers of the inmates. What is this century, to take the sneakers away, to leave an inmate bare footed so that he could put those sneakers on or shoes. When we got to Manjaca, it was dark and the camp would not admit us. We slept on Manjaca. Everything was all right until late in the evening when the singing of the soldiers began and then battery began again, screams. Each one of us experienced, saw it in his own way, but one had to go through it. In the morning, when the dawn broke out they let us off those buses. I do not know how many people died, cramped, and they were taken out from the buses on to the clearing in front of the buses; and we were sitting there. They cut the throats of several more people but I did not see it; other inmates saw that. I entered Manjaca toward the evening only.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Seferovic, I am sorry, I am not going to go into any details of Manjaca with you so that is why I interrupted you. I shall just have a couple more questions for you. You have told us about knowing Dule Tadic since you were a child and he was a child. Can you look around the courtroom, please, and tell us if Mr. Tadic is here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you point him out, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the gentleman up there. (Indicated).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that the man with the dark hair wearing the blue jacket and tie?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Seferovic, are you absolutely certain that this is the man you saw at the church slaughtering Osman and Edin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am certain. Yes, I am certain that this is the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is all I have, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Will there be cross-examination, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Seferovic, you have told the court about leaving Kozarac on the day of the shelling of that town, and going to stay in the land behind Kozarac towards Besici, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told the court earlier today that you think you were staying in that area for about three days after the shelling and then you returned to Kozarac to see what was happening and it was on that day that you saw the incident at the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You could not remember precisely the date when the attack on Kozarac took place, but you remembered it was a Sunday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was a Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you were outside Kozarac during that time when the town was still being shelled, were you on your own or with other people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Naturally with other people in the hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Presumably, there was a large number of people up there in the forest behind Kozarac with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a large number of people in the woods and the hills, in the basements. Besici were shelled the least.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The day that you went back into Kozarac and went to your brother's house, can you remember which day that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When Kozarac surrendered, I also do not remember what day it was, but I know that it was a nice day and that people surrendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Presumably, a lot of people surrendered at different times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, different times and a lot of people surrendered because Kozarac could not be taken over in one day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you said three days after the shelling, would that have been the Wednesday that you went back into Kozarac to your brother's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you help me with which day it would have been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was a Tuesday, but I do not remember, I think it was a Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I know a lot of chaos and despair occurred amongst the people who were outside Kozarac but, if possible, I want to try to identify this particular day that you say you saw Dusko Tadic kill these two men. Perhaps we can retrace your steps and if that helps you to identify the day, it will be of great importance, do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You left fairly quickly on the Sunday when the shelling started, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, very, very soon because Besici are not far -- Besici, the village of Besici, is not far from Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You went up to stay in Besici to avoid what was happening down in the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you able to see the shelling of Kozarac from where you were in Besici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because Besici is on the hill and Kozarac is in the plain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember how long the shelling took, how many days the shelling took of Kozarac? Was it just that one day, the Sunday, or was there shelling on the next day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they shelled Kozarac all the time until the people surrendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you able to tell me how many days that was that Kozarac was shelled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Even after Kozarac surrendered it was constantly shelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you went to Besici, did you stay in a house there or did you stay outside in the woods?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was in a house, in a basement, because this is a hillside area and it is easy to dig out a basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were there other people in that basement with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were other people, my family, brothers or sisters-in-law, children were there. I have four brothers and the three of us were in Kozarac and one lives in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So would it be right to say that this building in Besici was somewhere where your family also lived, another part of your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not live there. This is our -- this is the family of our acquaintances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you stay in that basement, the first night, the Sunday, that the shelling started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not. I went back to Kozarac. I took some personal belongings that I needed the most, my underwear, my shirts -- and I really needed them when I was wounded because I used that to tie my leg. I did not have any bandages or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So, although the shelling was taking place on Kozarac on the Sunday night, you went back into Kozarac to get some of your personal belongings, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the mortars were falling and I went to get my personal belongings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You got your belongings then that first night. Did you stay that night in Kozarac or did you return to Besici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I went back to Besici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You went back to the place that you had been during the day of the Sunday, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: During the next day, which would be the Monday, did you remain in Besici, in the basement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, not all the time. I went and took to the people food and blankets. There were women, children, elderly there. There was a large convoy of people. It was terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: During that day, the Monday, when you were giving blankets and other things to people, was the shelling of Kozarac still happening down below?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, not just Kozarac, but also surrounding towns that belong to Kozarac, to Muslim population -- and Croatian, Croat population. I forgot to mention that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the second night, that Monday night, did you remain in Besici or did you visit Kozarac again during the night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I remained in Besici. I spent the night in the basement. I slept on a hay -- I do not quite remember, yes, it was hay. We had blankets, naturally. I did not go home because I was afraid -- we were afraid of the shells because each shell went right through the house. There was not a house left that was not -- that the shell did not go right through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next day, which would be the Tuesday, after you had spent the night in the basement, did you remain in Besici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, in the morning I came home. I fed my birds. That was at dawn. I do not remember what hour exactly, but it was dawn. I fed my birds. I poured a lot of water for them, gave them a lot of seeds because I realised that I could not come back every day to feed the birds. Then I went back to Besici again, naturally with bread and blankets and other necessities because the houses were just filled with things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Presumably, you returned to the place where you had been staying before in Besici, to the basement, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not remember, but it was not just one basement, or one convoy of people. There were more people there. The largest convoy was between Kozarac, kamenje, and I also went to visit that convoy and I took them food and blankets and I do not know what else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again there would have been a large number of people, would that be right, in the hills and wood behind Kozarac sheltering from what had happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So, having fed your birds at dawn, you left Kozarac and you went back up into the hills and again gave out some of the blankets and supplies that you had been able to take?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That night, on the Tuesday night, can you remember whether you stayed in the basement or whether you stayed elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On Tuesday?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After you had fed -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember if Kozarac had already surrendered at that time, if it was Wednesday or not. It took several days for Kozarac to surrender. 26,000 people cannot leave the town in a day. This is why I do not remember what day it was when Kozarac surrendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if we take you through the steps that you took, what happened to you, we may be able to identify the day. You have told us about feeding your birds on the Tuesday morning, and taking more provisions away and taking them up to the people in the hills. Did you return into Kozarac that same day having fed your birds in the early hours of the morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not remember, but I think that I was in Kozarac on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So when you fed your birds in the early hours of Tuesday morning, presumably, you had fed them so that they would have enough for a few days, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you return to those birds again to see that they were fed and watered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, but I did go back constantly to the house to see the birds. Even after Kozarac surrendered, I did that and afterwards. I always went back home and paid attention to the birds, not just mine alone, but also my neighbour's.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But having taken things from your house in the early hours of Tuesday morning to give to other people, those would have been people up in the hills behind Kozarac, would they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Having done that did you go and see your family again? Did you see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On Tuesday?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw my brother, my younger brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you see him at the basement where you had previously stayed during the shelling of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was underneath the stones and this is why I went frequently up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Having seen your younger brother, did you stay that night out of Kozarac up in the hills?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I personally spent every night in the basement, or mostly in the basement or outside than in the hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So when you say you went back into Kozarac to your brother's house which was near the hospital, was that on the Wednesday, the day after you had fed your birds in the morning, or was it on the same day that you had fed them at dawn on Tuesday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not remember what day it was when Kozarac surrendered, but when Kozarac surrendered I went to see my brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you went to your brother's house, did you go alone or were you with anyone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your brother's house is in that road leading up from the church to the hospital, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could look at photograph 222B and a copy of it placed before the witness? Your Honours do not have copies of these, I take it, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No, we do not have them yet, but if you want to they can be put on the overhead projector, if that is needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, could it be put on the projector?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My brother's house was above this van, the first house to the left, above the bend towards hospital, the first house to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We can see there a van parked in the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us about how many metres from the church that would be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 60, 70 metres, I do not know exactly. I think it is what I told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it about halfway up the road between the church and the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is closer to the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you remember what time of the day it was when you got to your brother's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in the early afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was happening in Kozarac when you were there at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All people were going to the gathering point, and that is a road that is parallel to Prijedor/Banja Luka highway, and this old road where the church is is parallel, where the church and the house are, is parallel and that is the old road, and this one below is the new road and it is parallel to this road that goes to Prijedor or Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could look at the plan 220 you can identify for us where the gathering point was, and put it on the overhead projector. There you can see that on this plan -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the gathering point is -- this is the gathering point, people were directed towards Prijedor from all over Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that road you indicated where the gathering point was the new Banja Luka/Prijedor highway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the new highway Prijedor/Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How did you know that that was the gathering point down there where people were to meet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was because I saw it personally myself. I was at the sawmill and that is my company. It is located below the field and it is next to the highway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could indicate on this map then where the sawmill is? Can you do that with the pointer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The sawmill is here. This is the area where it is. It is -- there is just one house between the field and the sawmill. It is -- this house is next both to the field and to the sawmill.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you go down to there, towards the sawmill?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was at the sawmill, yes. I did go to visit my facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So, at what stage did you go to the sawmill after you had been at your brother's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not remember when I was at the sawmill, but I know that I was there because I took a lot of cans because there was a storage and everything was shelled, so the cans were all over the road and this is what saved my life probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am asking you about the time you went to Kozarac and you went to your brother's house and you told me that that was in the early afternoon, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told me that people were moving towards a collection point and you indicated that the collection point was ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- the new Banja Luka highway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I asked you how you knew that that was the collection point and you told us because you could see it as you went down to the sawmill which was where you used to work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I was not at the sawmill that day when I was by the church. I just do not remember what day it was because, as I said, Kozarac could not have surrendered in one day. It took several days for it to surrender. I do not remember how many days because I was wounded and I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let us go back a stage then. Perhaps you can think again and tell me how you knew on the day you went to your brother's house that people were moving to the collection point on the new Banja Luka highway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was just known because everybody was talking about it, people were going up and down and it was just a pure chaos. People did not know what to do. Everyone was hurrying here and there. It was just a pure chaos. Some people were going back in the evening; some people were going down. The buses could not take in all these people. I was desperate but I knew that everybody was going towards Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you were not walking around on the main streets, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. I did not use the main streets. Kozarac has many side streets, back yards, through which one can go from one neighbour to the other, and that is what I used mostly. Sometimes I did use the high street. I did not care whether I would be killed or stay alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But when you were moving around Kozarac on this day you went to your brother's house, you were on your own, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was on my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you meet and talk with any other people in Kozarac as you were moving around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, as I said, Kozarac was surrendering, thousands of people, I said, but I did not talk to anyone. I said I was looking for my family, for my brother who is no longer with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you moving around the back yards and back gardens and side streets because you did not want to be seen by anyone, you did not want to be captured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sometimes tanks, would pass by or amoured cars, I do not know what they called them, amoured vehicles, would pass into Kozarac, and I had to get away but I was not getting away from my people. I still love my people to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was there any reason why you did not go to the collection point down there on the highway, why you chose not to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. Something happened to me, something broke down and I said: "I will not go".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were people moving in a convoy or in groups through those streets of Kozarac down to the area, you said, at the Banja Luka highway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, people were going in every way possible, by cars, tractors, trucks, on foot, in carts, in wheel carts, old people, children and who knows how else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you see them on this day that you went to your brother's house moving like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. People were surrendering for many days. I do not know how many, but many, many, many days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was there a collection point in front of the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I would not know that. I do not think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you were going through the back yards and gardens down to the orchard after you had been to your brother's house, you said that you could see the church clearly from where you were in the orchard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I could see the church clearly, all too clearly, because there were leaves all over. The grass was a metre, a metre-and-a-half, tall. The hedge around the ground, the branches of plum trees, bending down to the ground. So that I could move as I liked and nobody, nobody could really see me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Those things would also stop you seeing clearly if you have to look through grass or trees, branches, hedges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. No, I was not moving then. I had found a spot and I had a good view. Nobody was paying attention to me, but to the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How long did you remain then in this position in the orchard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not long, the incident happened perhaps a few minutes after I arrived. I did not have a watch so .....

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After the incident happened did you leave straightaway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, straightaway because there was very intensive fire and bullets were whistling by.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Bullets were whistling by where you were in the orchard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, when this incredible fire started, then I beat a retreat. It is not an orchard. It is plum trees. I call it an orchard because Kozarac is all fruit trees all around.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the position that you have put yourself in where this orchard is, is it at the end of the street and past the houses; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Behind the houses, no. In front of the house which overlooks the churchyard and the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There was no house between you and the orchard and the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was a road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You had moved a considerable distance down from your brother's house, had you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as I was walking towards the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: About how many houses would you have passed to get from your brother's house down to the orchard at the end of the street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I should say six, I would not know the exact number, but I think six, I am not sure, but six.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you able to say how far from the house where your brother lived down to the orchard where you were, how far that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some 50, 60 metres. I have never measured it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Down there in front of the church there was no collection point that would have obscured your view?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, it was not the collection point but people were passing by.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No gathering of Muslims there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, except the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the only people then in that spot by the church were police and Serb troops or Serb paramilitaries, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told us earlier today about a group of civilians passing by the street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but soldiers had rifles. The rifles were aiming at them. They had to turn their head away and pass by the church, and they were heading for Krkici and hurried down to the main road, to the highway of Banja Luka/Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So how many Muslim policemen were there down by the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About six, I think it was about six.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How many of the others were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, nobody else was there but the police, Serb police, and Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How many Serb police and Serb soldiers were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my knowledge, when I saw them there were six policemen and Serb soldiers, so I do not know, up to 15. I did not count them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So not a group of about 50 people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: By the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, people were not moving in groups. They were in columns, family after family, neighbour following the footsteps of a neighbour. They almost all held hands. They were moving in a very wide front.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you remember making a statement about these matters for the Prosecution last year on 4th May 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were interviewed by a man with an interpreter called Aida, do you remember that, Aida Jahic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember that after you were interviewed your statement taken by them was read back to you in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you remember that you signed a certificate about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would you like to see a copy of that statement in your own language of Serbo-Croat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, if it is necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to draw your attention to something in that statement. I tender this before the witness, your Honour, as Defence 14, I think it is. (Defence Exhibit 14 was handed to the witness). That is a copy of the statement in your own language there that has been provided in that form. If you turn to the next page, Mr. Seferovic, you will see that the first paragraph gives your personal details about living in Kozarac; the second paragraph about the contact you have had to give evidence before this Tribunal; the third paragraph dealing with Sunday, 24th May 1992, can you see that paragraph? Can you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I think that the attack on Kozarac and surrounding villages began on Sunday 24th, on 25th May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. I do not need to go through that paragraph with you, but I would just ask you to look at the paragraph after that which is the fourth paragraph, on that same page. If you could turn back a page and look at that long paragraph that starts there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The last paragraph where you wish to tell of a specific incident. Just read it to yourself. Have you had a chance to read all that paragraph on that page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could I read this? No, I have not read this paragraph until now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That was a paragraph that would have been translated back to you in your own language on the day that you had been interviewed and given a statement to the Prosecutors.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did give -- I did make this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you say that your brother's house was about 100 metres from the Serbian orthodox church in the centre of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I may have and maybe it is that far. I said I never measured the distance; it could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you say that you only moved some 30 metres from your brother's house to a small orchard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I said that the house, that is, was about 30 metres or more from the orchard to the church. That is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you say that you were walking closer to a collection point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Because what I am suggesting to you is that you have made up this story about seeing this incident in the afternoon in Kozarac in front of the Serbian orthodox church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not invent it. I saw it with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say the Muslim policemen were in a line, were they standing against the wall of the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I think so, but one could see them all. They were to the side of me so that I could see them more from the profile most, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we look at photograph 222A -- if a copy could be put on the screen by the witness -- you say that that photograph there shows the orchard where you were hiding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the small orchard. You see, I told you that Kozarac is all made of fruit trees and I have always claimed that and I claim it today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In this patch of land here we have a great number of trees, do we not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Not only that, there is a thick hedge growing all the way around the ground, is there not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is some six, seven houses down from where your brother's house is, perhaps more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Six, six houses away from my brother's towards the hospital, towards the hospital, from this first house here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you had moved only 30 metres from your brother's house, you would still be up where the houses were, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, I did not say that. I said that I had moved 30 metres away from my brother's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you had only gone that distance though, would it not be right that you would be in the houses still in that street that leads from the church up to the hospital, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you had only moved 30 metres though from your brother's house, you would still be amongst those houses in the street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, but I was not walking down the street and I did not say I had got 30 metres away because there is more than that. There are six houses between my brother's house and this front house, and I was standing there in front of that house, and those naturally fruit trees, fruit trees and hedges; and at that time there was dense foliage and here we see it all naked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, and that is why I suggest to you that you would not have had a clear view in relation to any events occurring within the grounds of the churchyard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I had chosen a lovely viewpoint. I was some six or seven metres in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So there were soldiers who had told Muslims ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- civilians not to watch what was happening and you were brave enough to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, they were not talking, they were simply brandishing their rifles and turning them upwards, indicating to move towards Krkici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So how many people were walking down that road between the churchyard and the orchard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some 40 to 60 people. I do not know. I did not count. I had no time to count them. I paid no attention to people who were passing by. My attention was riveted on what was happening before the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were only down there for a few minutes, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not say I was several minutes there. I had come a few minutes before the murder of Kozarac policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After you say you saw the murder, you say that you left quickly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the murder this incredible, terrible fire began. I do not know from where and against whom, but the bullets were whistling by so I retreated behind the house and headed for the Besici hill in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So that is right when I put it to you that you said you were down there for only a few minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I said I had come several minutes before the incident. I do not know how long I stayed there, I paid no attention, but it seemed to me I was there for an infinite period of time when I saw all the provocations, slaughter, fire and then, I do not know, I do not know what I did. I simply turned my back on it. I was desperate and I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Any slaughter that you say would have taken place like that, would have involved a lot of blood pouring out, is that right? You say both men were cut across the throat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was towards the neck. Whether they were slaughtered, I do not know, but, yes, blood was gushing forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, that is what you said to us happened. You said that Osman had his throat cut and then was stabbed below several times.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did not count how many times ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And if ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- but I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If Edin had the same thing happen to him, as you said, his throat was cut as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same thing happened to Edin. I saw a thrust higher up and then the complete confusion began and this fire started, and I said to myself "I am desperate". I stood for a little while longer and then I turned and left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So was Edin's throat cut as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw a blow upwards. Of course he was, his throat was cut as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you see blood spill from both of these attacks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw the blood. Naturally one could see blood. When the firing started I stood there for a while and then I left. I had no time to continue watching any more; not that I did not have time; I could not continue watching any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So when you say Mr. Tadic did this amongst the group of Serb policemen to the Muslim policemen, did he grab Osman from behind or in front?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Osman and Edin stood next to each other. I think that Osman stood behind Edin, I think, and he grabbed him towards himself, he pulled him towards himself, and then the blow came and the next blows.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the blow was at the front of Osman's body into the neck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And presumably blood would have spurted forwards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, naturally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So we would expect anyone to be covered in blood if they had done that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so, because this is the neck and this is where the blood vessels are. I think that a lot of blood, a lot of blood burst out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You say that originally Osman was behind Besic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so. Edin was most visible because he was a very large man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When Esek was, you say, killed by Mr. Tadic, stabbed by him, was he grabbed from the front?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Edin, not Esek. Yes, yes, the blow also came, was directed upwards and I think he did the same to Edin. There was a tremendous shooting when this happened and I mentioned a hundred times and I will say a hundred times I was shocked. I stood there for a few seconds, I do not know how long, and then I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How soon after the group of civilians had passed down the road did this take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This all lasted for a few minutes. The civilians could still be seen on the road as they were heading towards Krkici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This was at a time when many people, thousands of people, were moving around Kozarac going to the collection point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again so it is clear, what I suggest to you is that you have made this up; you did not see this at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not make this up. I saw this with my own eyes and this is what I claim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Seferovic, let me talk to you briefly about that statement that Mr. Kay asked you about. First of all, when you talked with the Tribunal Investigator did he have any photographs of the area where your brother's house was or where the church was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he did not have any photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he have any map of the area ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he have any photographs of the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he did not have a map. He only had this picture that is on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The person who came to see you in 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he did not have anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then let me go through this very quickly using the photographs we now have and the map we now have. If we could put 220 back on the screen. Can you point out again where the collection point was at the Prijedor/Banja Luka highway for the court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards Prijedor, all the people were coming to this point here, from all over and then they were sent to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you point out again where your brother's house was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicated).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the church is in between?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was closer to the church than to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So the church is in between your brother's house and where the collection point was, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I said that my brother's house is between the church and the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is correct, but as you move from your brother's house toward the church, that also takes you closer to the collection point, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was getting closer to the house that is right in front of the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. Just taking it step by step, sir, if we were just to go down the map and if we were looking at a map as we are now, we would see that your brother's house is on the street between the hospital and the church, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You move to a point closer to the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. Then if one were to continue, for example, down that path past the church ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would come to the road, old road between Prijedor and Banja Luka, and this road served as the other -- it was used for the same purposes as other roads in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. Just down this road is where the collection point was at the junction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the intersection which was a turning by the field and the sawmill and led to the main street, main road between Prijedor and Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Of course the church is closer to that point than your brother's house is?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I do not mean to cut you off, but it is a little past 5.30 and we do need to adjourn today promptly. How much longer do you have with this witness? It is weekend and I know you would like to send him home.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I really would, your Honour, and I will try to cover it quickly. I do not know what the Court's schedule is. I presume that you would give me that leeway unless there was something pressing. If it is possible to do so I would like to continue.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, the question was, the church is closer to the collection point than your brother's house is, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the church is closer to my brother's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK, thank you, sir. What it says in your statement is from your brother's house: "... I walked closer to the collection point." If you can look at the words in that statement.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will assume that that is what the statement says.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is OK, sir, you do not have to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, did you also tell the Tribunal Investigator that you sought safety and cover in a small orchard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you also tell him from that position in the orchard you had an unobstructed view of the activity going on in front of the Serb church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is the view which is available from the position you showed us in the photograph, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: From that position you saw approximately 15 Serbian paramilitary soldiers, approximately six Muslim policemen and you also saw civilians passing by, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. You did not have a photograph so that you could show the Tribunal representative exactly where the policemen were or exactly where the Serbian paramilitary soldiers were, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, I did not have.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But you showed us on the map today, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, and I was very confident about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You were also able, using the photographs, to explain exactly where the civilians were passing by on the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right. What you told the Tribunal representative, is it not, is that you saw about 50 people in total: six, approximately six Muslim policemen, approximately 15 Serbian paramilitary soldiers and the rest Muslim civilians, is that correct? That is what you told them and that is what is in the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim civilians were passing by the church at the time when Muslim policemen stood in the yard of the church. This is what I said and I am firm about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is what you told him and it is reflected in this statement that you observed about 50 people total, including six Muslim policemen and so on. Then you also explained in the statement ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir? Did you see about 50 people total, civilians, the police officers and Serbians dressed in paramilitary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I did not count people that were passing by. I said I saw the people. It is impossible to count up the people in the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. Then you described to the Tribunal representative how Dule Tadic killed the two policemen just as you described it here in court and that is reflected in the statement, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is all I have, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, no further questions of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You have no further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. Any objection to Mr. Seferovic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour, before he is excused there are two quick matters. I understand that 221 is marked, is in evidence, is that right? That was the document there was a slight debate about whether or not to mark and I want to make sure it was in as marked.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Bos, is it in evidence? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As marked. Good. I do not believe at any point -- I believe the record should reflect the witness's identification of the accused which we ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Did I not say that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The record should reflect that Mr. Seferovic identified the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit 14 was marked for identification purposes and I gather you do not wish to offer that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I did not tender it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Are there any additional matters now? Are all of exhibits marked, Mr. Bos, in evidence except for Defence 14? OK, very good. Mr. Seferovic, you are permanently excused. You are free to leave. Thank you for coming. You may leave now. Let me remind Counsel that we will begin this matter on Tuesday at 11.30 a.m. because we have two initial appearances that we have to handle before we continue this trial. So the Court will adjourn until 11.30 on Tuesday.

procedural_notes.text: (The court adjourned for a short time)
(The court adjourned for a short time)
